command_bytes_delta_review.scope: Read-only review of changed SQL sections against prior pinned source. No product/test/service/SQL execution.
changes: Named binding_start_window_shape and binding_run_shape CHECKs without weakening predicates.
Removed the incorrect claim that G4 accepts U+0000; original ingress rejects NUL and no validation was relaxed.
Removed whole-command PostgreSQL JSON parsing so supported ASCII-escaped lone surrogate title/request_text need not be decoded by PostgreSQL.
Retained original canonical stored-byte envelope SHA and checks exact adjacent canonical profile/project/release key boundary using identity_bytes.
substring_boundary_proof: The exact existing CreateJob schema has eight fixed keys. Python sort_keys canonical order places profile_version, project_id and release_mode consecutively. The body is produced by G4 create_payload strict DTO plus payload_identity/ascii_json, not caller-controlled serialized SQL text.
Every scalar field except input_artifact_ids is a string, and input_artifact_ids contains canonical UUID strings. No accepted nested object can create another structural profile/project sequence.

Inside a JSON string all literal double quotes and backslashes are escaped by the canonical encoder. Therefore the raw comma-plus-unescaped-quote key boundaries in identity_bytes cannot be forged inside title/request_text/another string. A closing string quote cannot match the complete sequence because valid JSON requires a comma or object end immediately afterward.

catalog.profile_version_json is the already imported canonical ASCII string literal; h2_json_string renders the valid project string with the same ASCII escape form. Both values are non-null schema fields, so identity_bytes cannot silently become NULL. An exception resets expected_hash to NULL; comparison against non-null stored payload SHA rejects it.

Hashing the complete immutable stored body inside the exact original format/payload envelope preserves all free text bytes, including allowed lone surrogate escapes, without PostgreSQL JSON interpretation. The hash is integrity consistency, not proof of an untrusted producer.
trust_and_change_boundary: This boundary check is not an independent JSON/schema/canonicality validator for arbitrary SQL-inserted bodies. It relies on the existing trusted G4 ingress fixed DTO and immutable command origin. Possession of a compromised API runtime SQL credential allows arbitrary initial inserts and remains outside this guarantee, as with the existing auth/inbox boundary.

Any future accepted nested object, renamed/extra keys, canonical encoder change, profile-version representation change or alternate command producer invalidates this proof and requires reviewed replacement/extension. Non-create routes never use reserve_execution.

Actual runtime SQL/Python agreement must cover quote/backslash boundary-shaped user text, Unicode/astral characters, supported lone surrogates, mismatched profile/project and original NUL422/no-row behavior before acceptance.

producer_boundary_evidence: SnapshotBridge.decode_frame checks record structure/project/profile/workflow against exact requested identity and WORKFLOW constants; Node remains authoritative for original B01 canonical/hash semantics.

JobService.capture obtains that configured trusted bridge record, then bind_snapshot checks requested project/profile and all nine catalog fields against it before atomically accepting job+command+outbox.

catalog.import_snapshot only inserts the same nine-field trusted record; existing row mismatch fails rather than replacing it. Operator can INSERT but has no UPDATE/DELETE of profile_catalog. Runtime/dispatcher/projector similarly lack those mutations.

An operator-inserted arbitrary catalog row cannot become a genuine accepted API job unless it equals the independently captured trusted record. Merely supplying a matching stored raw hash is not claimed as Node validation or attestation.

Thus removing repeated SQL JSON inspection preserves the existing trusted producer responsibility while permitting already supported lone-surrogate profile versions. It does not add a new untrusted general-JSON acceptance path.
constraints_and_change_boundaries: Guarantee applies to jobs genuinely admitted by trusted G4 or an explicitly equivalent reviewed producer, with immutable catalog/job origin. Compromised runtime SQL credentials, schema owner mutations or arbitrary directly inserted jobs remain outside this boundary.

Future alternate ingress/direct-import job creation, mutable catalog grants or a changed bridge/workflow contract require renewed provenance and admission review. SHA consistency alone is insufficient for an arbitrary new producer.

Actual Node-to-import-to-HTTP202-to-SQL reservation/activation with escaped lone profile_version is required before the revised schema subgate can be accepted; existing G2-only bridge evidence does not prove this full path.
